title: Print a Student Record
description:
A `struct` groups related variables. Define `struct Student { char name[21]; int roll; int marks; }`, read one student, and print it.

Input
One line: `name roll marks` (name is a single word).

Output
Print `Name: <name>, Roll: <roll>, Marks: <marks>`.

title: Squared Distance Between Points
description:
Define `struct Point { int x, y; }`. Read two points and print the squared distance `(x1-x2)^2 + (y1-y2)^2`.

Input
One line: `x1 y1 x2 y2`.

Output
Print the squared distance.

title: Compare Two Rectangles
description:
Define `struct Rect { int w, h; }`. Compute the area of two rectangles and report which is larger.

Input
One line: `w1 h1 w2 h2`.

Output
Print `First` if the first area is larger, `Second` if the second is larger, or `Equal`.

title: Total Marks of All Students
description:
Read `n` students into an array of structs and print the total of all their marks.

Input
First line: `n`. Then `n` lines: `name roll marks`.

Output
Print the total marks.
constraints: name is one word of at most 20 characters

title: Find the Topper
description:
Find the student with the highest marks. Marks are all different.

Input
First line: `n`. Then `n` lines: `name roll marks`.

Output
Print `name roll marks` of the topper separated by single spaces.

title: Pass a Struct to a Function
description:
Structs can be passed by value. Write `int volume(struct Box b)` that returns `l*w*h`.

Input
One line: `l w h`.

Output
Print the volume.

title: Modify a Struct Through a Pointer
description:
Write `void addBonus(struct Student *s, int bonus)` that adds bonus marks, never going above 100. Use the arrow operator `s->marks`.

Input
One line: `name roll marks bonus`.

Output
Print `name roll marks` after the bonus.

title: Add Complex Numbers with typedef
description:
Use `typedef struct { int re, im; } Complex;` and a function `Complex add(Complex a, Complex b)` that returns a struct.

Input
One line: `re1 im1 re2 im2`.

Output
Print `re im` of the sum.

title: Day Names with enum
description:
Define `enum Day { MON = 1, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT, SUN };`. Read a number 1-7 into an enum and print its name in uppercase 3 letters (`MON`...`SUN`), then `Weekend` for SAT/SUN or `Weekday` otherwise, on the same line separated by a space.

Input
One integer `d`.

Output
Print `<NAME> <Weekend|Weekday>`.

title: Add Time Durations
description:
Define `struct Time { int h, m, s; }`. Add two durations and normalise so that `0 <= m < 60` and `0 <= s < 60` (hours can grow).

Input
One line: `h1 m1 s1 h2 m2 s2`.

Output
Print `h m s` separated by single spaces.

title: Sort Students by Marks
description:
Sort an array of student structs by marks from highest to lowest. Students with equal marks must keep their original input order (use a stable sort such as insertion sort).

Input
First line: `n`. Then `n` lines: `name roll marks`.

Output
Print one student per line as `name roll marks`.

title: Employees Joined Before a Year
description:
Define `struct Date { int d, m, y; }` and `struct Employee { char name[21]; struct Date join; }` (a nested struct). Count and list the employees who joined strictly before year `Y`.

Input
First line: `n Y`. Then `n` lines: `name day month year`.

Output
First line: the count. Then the names (in input order), one per line.

title: Tagged Union Printer
description:
A `union` stores one of several types in the same memory. Use `struct Value { int type; union { int i; double d; char c; } u; }`. Type 0 = int, 1 = double, 2 = char. Read `n` values and print each according to its type: ints as `%d`, doubles with `%.2f`, chars as `%c`.

Input
First line: `n`. Then `n` lines: `type value` (for char the value is a single non-space character).

Output
Print each value on its own line.
constraints: Doubles have at most 2 decimal places and absolute value <= 1000

title: Search a Student by Roll Number
description:
Search an array of students for a given roll number.

Input
First line: `n`. Then `n` lines: `name roll marks`. Last line: the roll `r` to find.

Output
Print `name marks` of the matching student, or `Not found`.

title: Add Fractions in Lowest Terms
description:
Define `struct Fraction { int num, den; }`. Add two fractions and reduce the result using the GCD.

Input
One line: `n1 d1 n2 d2`.

Output
Print `num/den` in lowest terms. If the result is a whole number, still print `num/1`.

title: Bank Account Transactions
description:
Define `struct Account { int id; int balance; }`. Process transactions: `D` deposits, `W` withdraws. A withdrawal larger than the balance is rejected and the balance stays unchanged. Count rejected withdrawals.

Input
First line: `n m` (accounts, transactions). Then `n` lines: `id balance`. Then `m` lines: `id type amount` (`type` is `D` or `W`). All ids exist.

Output
Print `id balance` for each account in input order, then a final line `Rejected: k`.

title: Sort Students by Name
description:
Sort students alphabetically by name using `strcmp` (uppercase letters come before lowercase). Names are unique. Swap whole structs.

Input
First line: `n`. Then `n` lines: `name roll marks`.

Output
Print each student as `name roll marks`, one per line.

title: Football League Table
description:
Teams play matches. A win gives 3 points, a draw 1 each, a loss 0. Keep a struct per team with points, goals scored and goals conceded. Rank teams by points (high first), then goal difference (high first), then name (alphabetical via `strcmp`).

Input
First line: `m`. Then `m` lines: `teamA goalsA teamB goalsB`. Team names are single words; there are at most 20 distinct teams.

Output
One line per team in rank order: `name points goalDifference`.

title: Days Between Two Dates
description:
Define `struct Date { int d, m, y; }`. Compute the number of days from the first date to the second (the second is never earlier). Remember leap years: divisible by 4, except centuries unless divisible by 400.

Input
One line: `d1 m1 y1 d2 m2 y2`.

Output
Print the number of days between them.
constraints: The second date is on or after the first

title: Linked List of Structs
description:
Build a singly linked list with `struct Node { int val; struct Node *next; }`. Insert `n` values at the END of the list, then delete the FIRST node holding each of `k` given values (ignore a value that is not present). Free all nodes.

Input
Line 1: `n`. Line 2: `n` integers. Line 3: `k`. Line 4: `k` integers to delete.

Output
Print the remaining values separated by single spaces, or `Empty` if none are left.
